Drug Advocacy System Based on Sentiment Analysis for Pharmaceutical Scrutiny Using Machine Learning Patterns

A medication recommender system that predicts sentiment based on patient reviews using vectorization processes including Bow, TF-IDF, Word2Vec, and Manual Feature Analysis. Multiple classification algorithms were applied to recommend the best drug for a given disease. The Linear SVC classifier using TF-IDF vectorization achieved the highest accuracy of 93%, demonstrating the power of machine learning in pharmaceutical scrutiny.
Linear SVC on TF-IDF → 93% accuracy · Perceptron on Bow → 91% · LGBM on Word2Vec → 91% · Random Forest on manual features → 88%
Authors: Dr. M. Ajay Kumar · Sree Kamya · K. Kiranmai · K. Ujwala · J. Neeshitha
Industrial Engineering Journal · UGC CARE Group-1
Effective Detection and Classification of Brain Tumor Using Discrete Wavelet Transform

A new computer-aided design (CAD) technique for classifying brain tumours in MRI data. The proposed approach collects characteristics from brain MRI images by exploiting the Discrete Wavelet Transform's significant energy compactness property (DWT). The Wavelet characteristics are combined with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to categorise input MRI images. The proposed strategy exceeds other commonly used methods with an overall accuracy of 99.3%.
Overall accuracy: 99.3% · Sensitivity: 97.4–98.2% · Specificity: 95.5–96.1% · Dataset: Figshare (Cheng) — 233 patients, 3 tumour types
Authors: M. Ajay Kumar · Sree Kamya · K. Kiranmai · S. Pragathi
Dynamic Accident Detection and Alert System Using Arduino

An accident detection and alert system using Arduino, GPS Receiver, and GSM module to address the critical issue of individuals being left without assistance following a road accident. The GPS Receiver identifies the vehicle's location and direction, while the GSM module sends an SMS with Google Maps coordinates to the assigned contact. The system detects severe accidents using a vibration sensor and can also identify rollovers, providing immediate location data to rescue services.

Real-time accident detection via vibration sensor · Precise GPS location transmitted via GSM · Google Maps link sent to emergency contact · Rollover detection included · Effective in high-accident regions — India, Nepal, Bangladesh

Data & Performance Intelligence — what separates high performers from the rest
Performance is not luck. It is a measurable, repeatable pattern — and this study found it.

Combined Kaggle’s Employee Performance Dataset with real organisational observations. Multi-variable analysis examining training hours vs performance scores, manager rating correlation with team output, tenure vs performance patterns, and education as a predictor. Hero finding: the highest performing employees share three characteristics — structured training investment, high-engagement managers, and joining with clear growth intent. Intentional development beats raw experience every time. Built advanced DAX-powered Power BI dashboards and layered Python statistical analysis (correlation matrices, regression modelling). Translated findings into an actionable Performance Blueprint — a practical framework for identifying, developing, and retaining high performers.

AI-generated insights vs traditional BI dashboards in managerial decision-making

Many organisations are adding AI-generated insights to their BI tools. They clearly make decisions faster. But do they make them better? My capstone tests whether AI summaries help managers decide more accurately, or mainly more quickly, and when people trust the AI more than they should.

Business master's students and early-career professionals step into a manager's shoes and solve four realistic business cases. Each case is built on a synthetic company dataset with one objectively correct answer.

Each case is shown in a different format: a Power BI dashboard, an AI-generated summary, or both together. The study measures decision accuracy, speed, confidence, overconfidence, trust and mental effort, and tests whether data literacy reduces over-reliance on AI.
Cognitive Fit Theory: decisions improve when the format matches the task
Automation bias: the tendency to follow a system even when it is wrong
Algorithm aversion and appreciation: when people reject or over-trust AI advice
that advises organisations when to use dashboards, AI summaries or both, which safeguards help people catch AI errors, and what data literacy teams need to use AI features safely.
data collection in progress until 2 December 2026, with final submission in December 2026. Supervised at the American Institute of Applied Sciences in Switzerland.
